findings.claim: Shared Graph-enabled UAMI is not restricted to SQL MI consumers.
findings.evidence: Task 12 step 7 records that each member has Owner on its dedicated workload subscription and step 10 grants/checks Managed Identity Operator on the shared id-sqlmi-directory. A member with workload Owner can create or modify an identity-capable resource in that subscription; the shared identity's assign/action permission lets that resource attach id-sqlmi-directory. Once attached, the resource can request managed-identity tokens carrying the identity's Graph application permissions: User.Read.All, GroupMember.Read.All, and Application.Read.All. Those app-role grants are exercised as the service identity, not bounded by the deploying user's delegated token or by the fact that the user can read some directory information. The historical acceptance rationale (tenant users' default directory read and short-lived lab subscriptions) therefore does not constrain attachment, token availability, or the service principal's authorization. The plan's checks establish identity existence and assign/action only; the plan, iac contract, governance assignments, and policy-property map contain no effective rule restricting this UAMI to Microsoft.Sql/managedInstances. The 2026-10-07 owner override is preserved as a risk disposition, but there is no new override or technical attachment control in this review's authorized scope.
findings.impact: A compromised or intentionally member-controlled resource in any workload subscription can attach the shared identity and use its app-only Graph token outside the SQL MI C7 user-creation path. This creates a tenant-directory access path across the shared-services trust boundary; normal user directory visibility and the lab's short lifetime do not prevent service-identity token use or reduce its scope.

suggested_fix.proposed_edit: Keep the existing id-sqlmi-directory binding and Graph grants unchanged during this review. Route to B08 for an effective boundary that prevents member workload principals from attaching this identity to any resource type other than Microsoft.Sql/managedInstances, plus independently verifiable pre-deployment evidence that the boundary is enforced across member subscriptions. The current existence and assign/action preflight is not that boundary. If B08 cannot provide and evidence the restriction, keep Step 4 DRAFT and return to the owner for an authorized identity-isolation decision before deployment; do not treat the historical risk acceptance as technical closure.
